independent.summary: Escape inside GeneratorOverlay closes two layers at once: the overlay's own `@keydown.esc="tryClose"` (GeneratorOverlay.vue:2) emits `close`, which synchronously sets `generatorOpen = false`, and the same event then bubbles on to the window listener, so `closeTopLayer` sees the generator already closed and falls through to close the chat or the detail panel underneath — the exact double-close the item removed GraphView's listener to prevent, and the opposite of the spec's claim that the double call is "a no-op".

The conversation-rename input binds `@keydown.escape.prevent="cancelRename"` with no `stopPropagation` (unlike EntityEditor's tag combobox, which stops it), so Escape while renaming a conversation cancels the rename and then reaches the global listener, which closes the whole chat panel — one press doing two things.

`n` has no layer guard: pressed while the settings overlay, generator or graph is open (focus outside a text field) it calls `openEditor()`, mounting a "New Entity" editor invisibly beneath the overlay, so the user sees nothing happen and finds an unexpected panel after closing the overlay.

grades.reason: The designed behaviour is the reverse — `/` typed while a text field has focus is declined as a character (and the suite does cover that case for the search input), so an untested "focus moves from another input" path is not a defect but behaviour that must not happen.

Purely speculative and untrue of this code: `grep -rn "window.addEventListener" client/src` names only the composable, and the real double-close comes from GeneratorOverlay's subtree-scoped handler, not from a second global listener.
